gap.quote: Existing work on reward overoptimization shows that excessive optimization against an imperfect reward proxy can eventually reduce the true reward
Our setting adds a distinct source of misspecification: the optimization domain is itself defined by an imperfect safety proxy.
but it cannot determine which responses were wrongly admitted by a safety proxy.
Pessimistic inference can provide scaling-monotonic guarantees for reward overoptimization under suitable conditions

approach.quote: For constrained Best-of-N sampling, we derive finite-N bounds governed by the joint upper reward tails of safe and unsafe outputs within the proxy-feasible set.
We derive N-independent safety-hacking bounds under coverage control and study cPes as a concrete instance.
An exact finite-N decomposition separates exposure to unsafe-but-feasible responses from the probability that they outrank every safe candidate.

evaluation.quote: compare random feasible selection, CBoN, and cPes for N
we use the HarmBench classifier as the operational safety criterion and define a safety-hacking event as selecting a response that passes Llama Guard but is classified as unsafe by HarmBench.
Our evaluation uses 714 test and 179 validation prompts

l2.gap: Reward overoptimization is studied, but not when an imperfect safety filter defines the search domain.
l2.approach: Derive bounds on selecting unsafe outputs from reward tails and limit concentration with coverage control.
l2.evaluation: Compare selection strategies as the sample budget grows using an independent safety classifier.
l2.query_text: Inference-time pipelines sample many responses, filter them with a learned safety model, and return the highest-reward response. How do errors of the safety filter interact with reward maximization as the number of samples grows, and what theoretical bounds limit selection of unsafe outputs?
